_readme: DROP-IN: example Claude Code hooks. Copy the sibling `hooks/` directory to
`.claude/hooks/` in your repo (`chmod +x` the scripts), then merge the
`.claude/settings.local.json` (personal). Fill in the CHECKS array at the
top of check-on-stop.sh with your repo's real commands — ideally the single
'make check' named in CLAUDE.md. Run `.claude/hooks/test-hooks.sh` after any
edit; it asserts the guard blocks what it claims to.
The three hooks implement: (1) verification that always runs, (2) a gate on
WHY SCRIPTS AND NOT INLINE ONE-LINERS: hooks receive their payload as JSON
version of this template used them, which silently made every hook a no-op:
the guard grepped an empty string and exited 0 on every command. Two further
traps this template previously fell into: piping a check to `tail` reports
tail's exit status (0), so failures pass; and exit code 1 is NOT blocking in
Claude Code — only exit 2 blocks and feeds stderr back to the model.
Verify shapes against https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks before relying
on this; they occasionally change between releases.

hooks._purpose: Lint every edited file immediately. The model gets the error in-loop whether or not it would have checked.
Runs the check suite when Claude tries to finish, so a red suite surfaces at 'done' time instead of after merge. Blocks with exit 2; capped so an unfixable failure cannot trap the conversation.

Physics-level guard on irreversible commands: force-push (in any argument order), hard reset, recursive delete, branch force-delete, git clean, history rewrites, migrations, table drops. Extend the pattern list for your stack (e.g. terraform apply, kubectl delete).
